links.outcome: Rate of fabricated (nonexistent) references cited by LLMs in gastrointestinal pathology scenarios
links.effect: 25-50% of model responses cited references that do not exist (hallucinations); none of the models gave accurate TNM staging.
links.quote: None of the models could provide the accurate TNM staging for these clinical scenarios, with 25-50% citing references that do not exist (hallucinations).

screen.reason: The study tests the baseline diagnostic and reasoning performance of LLMs (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, Gemini Advanced) on 20 clinicopathological GI scenarios without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
